chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with the Mention of Allah while you are urinating, for the Mention of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is good in every state; therefore, do not tire of the Mention of Allah.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to recite Quran or dhikr while urinating in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while specific adab (etiquette) like avoiding the mention of Allah's name in the most impure states exists, general dhikr is permissible and virtuous during urination, emphasizing its continuous nature. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly view that dhikr is a pervasive spiritual practice rather than a ritual confined to specific postures, encouraging believers to maintain remembrance in all bodily states. The hadith serves to prevent excessive rigidity, affirming that the act of remembering Allah is inherently praiseworthy regardless of minor physical distractions.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘There is no problem with the Mentioning of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> while you are urinating, for the Mention of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is good upon every state. Therefore, do not hesitate from the Mentioning of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from al-Halabi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘It is not an offense to speak of Allah when you are urinating; speaking of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is good in all conditions. Do not feel embarrassed about it.’”
